publication.provenance: Original editorial synthesis of private project notebooks and experiment reports, with reviewed capture images, selected source excerpts and their provenance. Firmware, storage images, complete run artifacts and the implementation repository are not included.

record.title: The storage callback ABI crosses compiler conventions
record.method: Exact-build call-site inspection; ARM and Thumb receivers; negative control
record.observation: The measured completion convention splits its final 64-bit count between a register and the stack. The contemporary bare-metal EABI comparison places it differently. Synthetic receivers verify both words and register preservation; the ordinary-EABI control fails as expected.
record.limits: The probe isolates the boundary. It does not recover the full Darwin C++ ABI or exercise a physical storage device.

exhibits.interpretation: A 64-bit fourth argument is the discriminator. The probe used nonzero high and low words so an incorrect placement could not hide behind a short transfer.

excerpts.content: The embedded `IOBlockStorageDriver` calls the provider's legacy 64-bit asynchronous read/write slot with block in `r2/r3`, count in the first two stack words, and the three completion fields by value after it. Its completion helper invokes the action with target in `r0`, parameter in `r1`, status in `r2`, byte-count low word in `r3` and high word at the top of the stack. A normal EABI call with a 64-bit fourth argument places both words on the stack instead. The mismatch would corrupt a transfer's completion count even if its sector data were correct.
